attempts.summary: Enabled a persistent firewalld host firewall on node1 (RHEL 7.9): the public zone allows SSH and TCP/8080, all other inbound traffic is rejected (icmp-host-prohibited), and the config survives reboot. Verified via inspection that firewalld was already active/enabled with SSH permitted; added 8080/tcp permanently and reloaded. Confirmed the resulting iptables chains: IN_public_allow ACCEPTs only tcp/22 and tcp/8080, INPUT falls through to REJECT for anything else. Live cross-host packet testing wasn't possible because this is a single-node cluster (self-directed curl traffic to the node's own IP is short-circuited over the lo interface, bypassing the eth0-scoped zone rules entirely — confirmed via iptables packet counters), so correctness was verified by direct rule/chain inspection instead. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline (192f6cab...), issued a deferred `reboot` so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until SSH access returned, confirmed boot_id changed to 70e5b34e... (new boot time 2026-09-03 09:26), and verified firewalld was active/enabled with the same ssh+8080 rule set and REJECT-by-default chain intact post-reboot.
